name: Yapese
orthography_note: Ross's comparative transcription of Hsu (1969) and Jensen (1977a, 1977b) (Ross 1996: n. 3): c is the affricate written ch in Yapese orthography (value not stated by Ross; decision ross1996-symbols); y is the palatal glide (j here); a superscript ʔ marks a glottalised consonant (fˀ, vˀ), which Table 3 derives from *CVq.
notes: Western Micronesia; not Nuclear Micronesian. Ross (1996) separates five strata of Austronesian vocabulary: Sets A and B from non-Oceanic sources (an older stage of Palauan or a lect close to it; an unidentified conservative language), Set C from an Oceanic source outside Nuclear Micronesian, Set D and its variant Set UW from Nuclear Micronesian (mostly Western Trukic) and recent Ulithian and Woleaian loans, and a small Set E from a Central Pacific source (pp. 128-131). Set C is the inherited stratum: the bound morphemes reflect it, so Yapese is Oceanic (p. 130). Ross tentatively links its inherited stratum with the Admiralties, as an early offshoot (§2.3, pp. 143-151); there is no Admiralties node here. Every Yapese word must begin and end with a consonant, so a glottal stop is added to vowel-initial and vowel-final words (p. 131). Glottocode and coordinates from the language metadata of Ross et al. (2023).
